articles.title: Pittsburgh vs Florida State: Panthers Defense Battles, Falls 16-10 at Home
articles.matchup: Final: Florida State Seminoles (5-5) 16, Pittsburgh Panthers (6-4) 10, Fri., Nov. 13, Acrisure Stadium, Pittsburgh. Next: at Louisville, Sat., Nov. 21, time TBA, L&N Federal Credit Union Stadium, Louisville
articles.text:
Yinz, I'm not gonna sugarcoat it. Florida State 16, Pittsburgh 10 on Friday night at Acrisure Stadium, and the Panthers are 6-4. There were 45,734 of us bundled up on the North Shore, and we deserved a happier walk home across the river.

The defense showed up, I'll give 'em that. Florida State managed 260 yards, ran for just 97 on 33 carries and converted 3 of 13 third downs. Cruce Brookins was everywhere with 10 tackles. Braylan Lovelace forced a fumble and had a tackle and a half for loss. Early in the fourth, Alex Sanford Jr. knocked the ball loose from Ashton Daniels and Shawn Lee Jr. fell on it at our 6 to keep it a 13-10 game.

Our lone touchdown was a beauty. Corey Dailey moved us 85 yards in 10 plays late in the second quarter, hit Malik Knight for 28 deep down the left side and found Ja'Kyrian Turner for an 11-yard score to put us up 7-6 at the half. Turner finished with seven catches.

Then came the play that stung. On our second snap of the third quarter, a throw was intercepted at our 39, and five plays later Florida State was in the end zone. Antonio Chadha's 34-yard field goal pulled us to 13-10, but their kicker answered from 47 with 6:27 left.

We had our chances. Three times we went for it on fourth down and came up short, including a sack near midfield with 8:44 left. After a 64-yard punt pinned us at our own 2 with 1:49 to go, Dailey took off for 24 yards on the first snap and got us to their 48, but the last fourth-down throw fell incomplete with 43 seconds left. Dailey ran for 58 yards on nine carries and battled every snap.

Pittsburgh doesn't do quit. We're still 6-4, still 5-2 at home, and cold November football is our kind of weather. Three rivers, one city, and a whole lot of fight left in this bunch.

Next: at Louisville, Saturday, Nov. 21, kickoff time to be announced. Wear the blue and gold, make some noise on the road, and let's bring one home. Hail to Pitt.

articles.title: Florida State vs Pittsburgh: Panikowski and a Stingy Defense Win 16-10
articles.byline: Gianna Ravello, The Florida State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Florida State Seminoles (5-5) 16, Pittsburgh Panthers (6-4) 10, Fri., Nov. 13, Acrisure Stadium, Pittsburgh. Next: vs NC State, Sat., Nov. 21, 3:30 PM ET, Doak Campbell Stadium, Tallahassee
articles.text:
Garnet and gold just froze out Pittsburgh. Florida State 16, Pittsburgh 10 on Friday night at Acrisure Stadium, and the Seminoles are 5-5. I packed my one Tallahassee sweater for a November night on the North Shore, and I would wear it every week for wins like this.

Gabe Panikowski was the coolest man in western Pennsylvania. He hit from 37 and 27 yards in the first half, then drilled a 47-yarder with 6:27 left to make it 16-10. Three tries, three makes. Somebody put that young man's right leg in a museum.

The turning point came on Pittsburgh's second snap of the third quarter. We trailed 7-6 at the half, and Rylan Kennedy jumped a throw at the Pitt 39 and brought it back to the 32. Amari Thomas ripped off 16 yards on the very next play, and five snaps after the takeaway, Thomas punched it in from a yard out. 13-7, Noles, and I was hollering in a sea of Pitt gold.

Ashton Daniels kept the offense steady, going 16 of 24 for 163 yards with no interceptions. Jasen Lopez caught five balls for 72 yards, including a 46-yard grab down the left side that set up our second field goal.

But this one belongs to the defense. Pittsburgh converted 5 of 15 third downs and came up empty on three different fourth downs. Caleb LaVallee sacked Corey Dailey on fourth down near midfield with 8:44 left. Then Daniel Hughes boomed a 64-yard punt that pinned Pitt at its own 2 with 1:49 to go, and Charles Lester III broke up a deep ball on that last drive before the final fourth-down throw fell incomplete with 43 seconds left. Chris Jones led us with seven tackles, and CJ Richard Jr. and Ashlynd Barker had six apiece.

It wasn't pretty everywhere. We ran for 97 yards on 33 carries and lost a fumble at their 12 early in the fourth. A road win in Pittsburgh in November is a road win, though, and I will take gritty and happy every single time.

Next: NC State comes to Doak Campbell Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 21, at 3:30 PM ET. Sweater off, sunscreen on. Tallahassee, get loud.

articles.title: Colorado vs Houston: 28 Straight Points and a Stampede Onto Folsom Field
articles.matchup: Final: Colorado Buffaloes (4-6) 42, Houston Cougars (7-3) 32, Fri., Nov. 13, Folsom Field, Boulder. Next: at Cincinnati, Sat., Nov. 21, 12:00 PM ET, Nippert Stadium, Cincinnati
articles.text:
The kids rushed the field at Folsom, and I was right behind them with my knees creaking. Colorado 42, Houston 32 on Friday night in Boulder. The Buffaloes are 4-6, and we just beat a top-15 team for the first time since 2007. The Flatirons were dark, the air was cold, and I have never felt warmer in my life.

It did not start pretty. Houston kicked a field goal, scored again seconds into the second quarter, and was up 20-7 after a 52-yard kick with 2:36 left in the half. I was muttering at the scoreboard. Then the Go-Go offense finally went, went.

DeKalon Taylor took one carry and turned it into a 67-yard touchdown with 1:49 left. JaQuail Smith ripped off a 32-yarder with 15 seconds on the clock, and suddenly we led 21-20 at halftime. Richard Young had already gone 38 yards for our first score, and he finished with 99 yards on 21 carries and two touchdowns. Colorado ran for 249 yards, the most of the Sanders era. Boulder, we can run the ball!

The third quarter was the knockout. Right after Randon Fontenette forced a fumble on Houston's first snap of the half, Isaac Wilson hit Joseph Williams for a 53-yard touchdown, and after Wilson limped off, Kaneal Sweetwyne scored on his very first snap, a 14-yard keeper that made it 35-20. Twenty-eight straight points. Wilson finished 17 of 25 for 217 yards, and he came back on that ankle, which tells you everything about the kid.

Randon Fontenette was the best player on the field on defense. Thirteen tackles, 12 of them solo, plus that sack that knocked the ball loose from Conner Weigman. Boo Carter picked off a throw late in the third. We converted 10 of 14 third downs, and that is how you keep a good offense on the sideline.

Houston kept coming. Weigman threw for 272 yards and three scores, and when they made it 35-26, my heart did a little dance I didn't enjoy. Young's 2-yard run with 3:59 left settled it.

Two more to go, Buffs. Ralphie's ready. So am I. The Colorado Buffaloes travel to face Cincinnati in Cincinnati, Nov. 21, noon ET.

articles.title: Houston vs Colorado: Weigman Battles, Cougars Fall 42-32 in Boulder
articles.matchup: Final: Colorado Buffaloes (4-6) 42, Houston Cougars (7-3) 32, Fri., Nov. 13, Folsom Field, Boulder. Next: at West Virginia, Sat., Nov. 21, time TBA, Milan Puskar Stadium, Morgantown
articles.text:
Coogs, I need a minute. Colorado 42, Houston 32 on Friday night at Folsom Field, and we're 7-3. I wore my red in the Boulder cold, I watched the Buffaloes fans pour onto the field, and I drove the long way back to the hotel so I could think about what happened between the last two minutes of the first half and the end of the third quarter.

Because for a while, this was our night. Jonathan Dimas opened with a 27-yard field goal. Makhi Hughes punched in an 8-yarder seconds into the second quarter. Conner Weigman hit Amare Thomas for a 4-yard score, and then Dimas drilled a 52-yarder with 2:36 left in the half. 20-7, Houston. The mountains looked friendlier at that moment.

Then it all slipped away. Colorado broke a 67-yard run, then a 32-yarder with 15 seconds left, and we went to the locker room down 21-20. On our first snap of the third quarter, Weigman got sacked and fumbled, and they cashed it in with a 53-yard throw. We came up empty on fourth down at their 25, then they added a 14-yard keeper, and that was 28 straight points against a defense I'd put up with anybody's.

I'm proud of how the offense answered. Weigman threw for 272 yards and three touchdowns. Patrick Overmyer was terrific with nine catches for 116 yards and a 22-yard score. Hughes ran for 106 yards on 15 carries, and Re'Shaun Sanford II added 70. Trent Walker caught a 4-yard touchdown with 1:51 left. We put up 477 yards in their building.

On defense, Kentrell Webb made nine tackles and Javion White picked off a throw to open the second half. But Colorado ran for 249 yards and converted 10 of 14 third downs, and nobody wins in the mountains giving up that.

This one stings because it was there for the taking. But this team is 7-3, Willie Fritz has built something real, and a single bad stretch in Boulder doesn't change that.

Bring a coat, Coogs. Then bring the fight. Go Coogs. The Houston Cougars travel to face West Virginia in Morgantown, Nov. 21, time TBA.

articles.title: UCLA vs Illinois: Scooter Jackson, Aidan Mizell and a Rain-Soaked 10-0
articles.matchup: Final: UCLA Bruins (10-0) 22, Illinois Fighting Illini (6-4) 14, Fri., Nov. 13, Rose Bowl, Pasadena. Next: at Michigan, Sat., Nov. 21, time TBA, Michigan Stadium, Ann Arbor
articles.text:
Ten and oh. Say it slowly, Westwood. UCLA 22, Illinois 14 on Friday night at the Rose Bowl, and the Bruins are 10-0 for the third time in program history. It rained in Pasadena, which basically never happens, and I stood in the Arroyo with a soggy blue poncho and the biggest grin in Southern California.

Let's start with Aidan Mizell, because the man refuses to be slowed by anything, rain included. Six catches, 176 yards. On our opening drive he hauled in a 54-yard touchdown from Ty Dieffenbach, and the whole stadium knew right away this was going to be his night.

Then came the scare. Dieffenbach went down on that elbow late in the second quarter and headed to the locker room, and I swear you could hear 45,800 people hold their breath at once. Madden Iamaleava kept the ship upright for three series. When Ty jogged back onto the field with 55 seconds left in the third, the noise was something I will tell my grandkids about. His first drive back went 75 yards in eight plays and ended with Semaj Morgan catching a 26-yarder in the end zone. 19-7, Bruins. Dieffenbach finished 13 of 20 for 232 yards and two scores. Warrior stuff.

But the best part of this whole wet night was the defense. Scooter Jackson picked off two throws, including the one with 2:50 left that he took back 41 yards to the Illinois 19. Derrick Barksdale grabbed another. Aiden Gobaira sacked Katin Houser in the end zone for a safety in the third quarter, and Sammy Omosigho led us with seven tackles. Illinois managed 240 yards and 64 on the ground. Seven straight opponents held to 20 points or fewer. Pasadena, that's a wall.

Mateen Bhaghani was perfect, too: a 20-yarder before halftime and a 37-yarder with 1:56 left that made it a two-score game. Curtis Gerrand dropped three punts inside the 20. Special teams win wet games.

Illinois never quit, I'll give the Illini that. They cut it to 19-14 with 7:14 to go, and I was not breathing again for a while. But this group just keeps finding a way.

Big House, big stage, 10-0 Bruins. Pack a sweater, Westwood. We're going to need it. The UCLA Bruins travel to face Michigan in Ann Arbor, Nov. 21, time TBA.

articles.title: Illinois vs UCLA: Illini Fight Back in the Rain, Fall 22-14 in Pasadena
articles.matchup: Final: UCLA Bruins (10-0) 22, Illinois Fighting Illini (6-4) 14, Fri., Nov. 13, Rose Bowl, Pasadena. Next: vs Iowa, Sat., Nov. 21, 2:30 PM ET, Gies Memorial Stadium, Champaign
articles.text:
Well, Illini Nation, we came to the Rose Bowl and it rained on us. Of course it did. UCLA 22, Illinois 14 on Friday night in Pasadena, and we're 6-4. I flew out of Champaign hoping for sunshine and palm trees and got a wet seat and a long walk back to the car.

The first half was rough, and there's no use pretending otherwise. UCLA hit a 54-yard touchdown on its first drive, kicked a field goal before halftime, and we went into the locker room down 10-0 without a point to show for our trouble. Then in the third quarter Katin Houser got sacked in the end zone for a safety, and it was 12-0. That's when you find out what a team is made of.

Ours is made of fight. Late in the third, Houser found Kaden Feagin for an 18-yard touchdown, and the orange in our corner of the stadium came alive. After UCLA answered, Houser marched us right back and hit Collin Dixon from 7 yards out with 7:14 left. 19-14. We were one stop and one drive from stealing one at the Rose Bowl.

James Kreutz played like a man possessed. Eleven tackles, three for loss, and he seemed to be in on every big stop. Matthew Bailey added nine tackles, Ismael Kante got a sack, and Clarke picked off a throw in our end zone in the second quarter to keep it close. That defense deserved better than this result.

The turnovers are what got us. Houser threw three interceptions, two to Scooter Jackson, and the last one came with 2:50 left and the game still in reach. UCLA kicked a 37-yarder at 1:56, and our last try ended on a fourth-down throw that fell incomplete. Hudson Clement had three catches for 62 yards and Aidan Laughery ran hard for 49, but against an unbeaten team, three giveaways are too many.

Here's what I know about this program. We went into the Rose Bowl against an unbeaten team and made them sweat into the final two minutes. We converted 8 of 16 on third down. Nobody packed it in.

Dry socks, loud voices. Oskee-wow-wow, Champaign. The Illinois Fighting Illini host Iowa at Gies Memorial Stadium, Nov. 21, 2:30 PM ET.
